decisions.rationale: Lead Farigiraf + Camerupt for the Trick Room route while Armor Tail suppresses priority disruption. Mega Camerupt can punish the confirmed sun core once Room is active; Heliolisk exploits sun and threatens Charizard, while Tauros supplies Intimidate and 4x Rock coverage into Charizard.
decisions.notebook: Opponent previously led Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Miracle Seed Venusaur and repeatedly used Solar Beam under sun. Confirmed Excadrill is Jolly Mold Breaker Focus Sash with Earthquake, Iron Head, Rock Slide, Protect; Mold Breaker limits ability-based counterplay and it threatens Mega Camerupt. Confirmed opponent members: Charizard Y, Venusaur, Excadrill; unrevealed fourth is Scizor, Toxapex, or Weavile. Charizard is 2x weak to Heliolisk Thunderbolt and 4x weak to Tauros Rock Slide; Venusaur is 2x weak to Floette Psychic. Preserve a credible Farigiraf Trick Room route before committing Mega Camerupt.

decisions.rationale: Charizard Protect+Mega sets Drought sun immediately, avoids friendly Fire from Excadrill's Earthquake, and keeps Charizard at full HP. Excadrill Earthquake hits both foes at 2× with Mold Breaker ignoring Solid Rock, likely OHKOing 4×-weak Camerupt before it can Mega Evolve. Sun synergizes with Venusaur and Charizard's Solar Beam for future turns.

decisions.rationale: Switching Tauros cuts Excadrill’s Earthquake damage via Intimidate, giving Mega Camerupt a much better chance to survive Charizard’s Solar Beam plus Earthquake and return an immediate 4x Ancient Power into Mega Charizard Y. Helping Hand leaves Camerupt exposed to the likely double target.

Excadrill carries Earthquake, Iron Head, Rock Slide, Protect; Intimidate remains valuable against it despite Mold Breaker. Charizard Y commonly enables Venusaur Solar Beam under sun. Mega Camerupt’s Sheer Force Ancient Power is 4x into Charizard and can OHKO with favorable rolls; Helping Hand makes the range substantially stronger. Preserve Trick Room when Camerupt can safely survive the setup turn. Remaining opponent slot is Scizor, Toxapex, or Weavile.

decisions.rationale: Bring both remaining Pokémon. Tauros immediately threatens Charizard with Rock Slide, while Farigiraf provides Armor Tail protection and a potential Trick Room route against the slower opposing core.
Fire Blast KOes 32% Tauros with SpA 211 + sun boost; Iron Head pressures full-HP Farigiraf to deter Trick Room setup. Eliminating Tauros now leaves a favorable 2v1.

Weavile's 194 Speed and IceShard priority let it OHKO Tauros at 32% regardless of Trick Room. Dark/Ice resists Farigiraf's Psychic STAB. Excadrill at -2 Attack is better off passing; its Earthquake spread can chip later.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand–boosted Rock Slide is the only immediate line that can remove Charizard-Y while also damaging Excadrill; Tauros is guaranteed ahead of Excadrill, and preserving both Pokémon if Charizard is not at the speed tie offers the best path through the remaining unrevealed backline.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Charizard-Y is Timid and can reach 167 Speed; Tauros is exactly 167, so their normal-priority order is unresolved if Charizard is fully invested. Excadrill is Jolly Mold Breaker Focus Sash and reaches at most 154, so Tauros always moves before it outside Trick Room. Charizard-Y has Fire Blast, Solar Beam, Air Slash, Protect; Excadrill has Earthquake, Iron Head, Rock Slide, Protect. Opponent’s likely sun back is Chlorophyll Venusaur; remaining possible roster includes Scizor, Toxapex, and Weavile. Farigiraf’s Armor Tail blocks opposing priority against its side. Prioritize removing Charizard-Y with Expert Belt Tauros Rock Slide, especially when boosted by Helping Hand; do not rely on Trick Room while Tauros is the fast remaining attacker.

reflections.summary: The series win was driven primarily by Excadrill running Focus Sash with Mold Breaker Earthquake/Iron Head, which cleanly survived Camerupt-Mega's Eruption on Turn 1 and OHKO'd it the same turn, then consistently landed critical Iron Heads throughout. The Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Venusaur) was the strongest pairing, making Charizard's Solar Beam free and amplifying damage. The opponent's team was fragile—Camerupt and Heliolisk fell in the same turn—leaving Farigiraf alone with only Trick Room as leverage. Zero decision errors and clean simulator play kept momentum. Charizard and Weavile both fell to opposing Rock Slide/Close Combat in the mid-game, but Excadrill's survivability and Venusaur's late-game Solar Beam under Trick Room closed out the match.
reflections.adjustment: Weavile fainted in Game 2 and was unavailable for the rest of the series; against this opponent's physical attackers (Tauros, Camerupt), consider whether Scizor or a bulkier sixth slot provides more staying power than Weavile's speed/priority. Toxapex was never fielded—test whether it offers better answers to Tauros and Farigiraf's Helping Hand combinations. Against Farigiraf Trick Room specifically, ensure Excadrill can threaten it before Trick Room activates or have Venusaur's Solar Beam already charging. Expect Liepard (Prankster Taunt/Encore/FakeOut) and Floette-Eternal next time—pack a Taunt-resistant answer or faster Taunt user.
reflections.notebook: EXCADRILL FOCUS SASH + MOLD BREAKER: survives Camerupt-Mega Eruption, OHKOs after Sash. Primary win condition vs this opponent. FARIGIRAF TRICK ROOM: key speed-control threat—eliminate before it fires or have Solar Beam already charging. CAMERUPT-MEGA: 4x Ground weak, Focus Sash Excadrill cleanly handles; do NOT let it set up. SUN CORE (Charizard Y + Venusaur): strongest pairing for this matchup; Charizard Solar Beam in sun is a free nuke. HELIOLISK: folds to any super-effective hit in Sun; not a long-term threat. TAUROS PALDEA COMBAT: Intimidate + Close Combat is dangerous—needs chip damage or priority to revenge kill; Excadrill crit Iron Head handled it. LIEPARD (Prankster Taunt/Encore/FakeOut) and FLOETTE-ETERNAL: likely remaining picks—prepare disruption answers or faster Taunt users. Toxapex and Scizor untested—evaluate if they improve matchup vs physical aggression and Trick Room teams.

reflections.summary: Game 2 was lost because the Camerupt-centered plan was exposed to Charizard Y + Mold Breaker Excadrill before Trick Room was established: Camerupt and the incoming Focus Sash Heliolisk both fell to Excadrill's Earthquake pressure, creating an unrecoverable material deficit. Tauros and Farigiraf still traded effectively—Tauros removed Charizard and Weavile while double-Intimidating Excadrill—but critical Iron Heads, plus the Rock Slide miss into Excadrill, prevented a comeback. Mega Camerupt was a poor Mega choice for this lead matchup without immediate Trick Room support. The evidence does not show the Game 1 plan or specific between-game adjustment, so it cannot establish why Game 1 was lost; Game 2's apparent Camerupt/Heliolisk adjustment backfired and clinched the 0-2 series loss.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, bring a coherent speed plan rather than exposing Mega Camerupt outside Trick Room alongside fast Tauros/Heliolisk. Do not default to Cameruptite into Charizard Y + Excadrill unless Farigiraf can establish and preserve Trick Room before Camerupt must absorb Earthquake. Prioritize a lead that pressures Charizard while keeping an Excadrill Earthquake from hitting two vulnerable allies; Tauros was valuable for Intimidate and its Charizard/Weavile coverage. Re-evaluate the four and Mega choice before the rematch: Camerupt was not justified by this game, while Farigiraf and Tauros were the clearly useful members. There is insufficient set evidence to claim that the unused registered members or omitted draft members would definitely have been better, but they should be compared specifically for a safer Excadrill matchup.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's Game 2 selection was Mega Charizard Y, Mold Breaker Focus Sash Excadrill, Expert Belt Weavile, and Chlorophyll Miracle Seed Venusaur; Scizor and Toxapex were not brought. Charizard Y is Timid with Fire Blast, Solar Beam, Air Slash, and Protect; its sun enables Venusaur speed and immediate Solar Beam while Charizard remains active. Excadrill is Jolly, has Focus Sash, and showed Earthquake, Iron Head, Rock Slide, and Protect; Mold Breaker means it is a major spread-damage threat even after Intimidate, though Tauros reduced it twice in this game. Weavile is an all-attacking Expert Belt set with Ice Shard, Night Slash, Icicle Crash, and Knock Off; Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks its priority Ice Shard while Farigiraf is present. Venusaur has Sludge Bomb, Solar Beam, Giga Drain, and Protect; Psychic Noise does not reliably OHKO full-health Venusaur. Tauros outspeeds Excadrill outside Trick Room, while Trick Room is chiefly a late-game Farigiraf option after Tauros is gone. Prep conclusion: preserve a real Trick Room route before committing Mega Camerupt, and account for Excadrill's Sash and Earthquake when choosing leads.
